page.title: Approvals
page.purpose: Show every charge waiting on a human and let the operator judge each one without opening a detail view. This is the landing surface because approval is the only workflow where the system is blocked on a person.

priorities.statement: Each pending request states its amount and counterparty before anything else
The operator can approve or decline from the list without navigating away
A request approaching its expiry is distinguishable from one that just arrived
The mandate and budget that admitted each request are identifiable in one glance
An empty queue reads as a healthy resting state, not as a failure to load

states.description: One or more requests are pending.
No request is pending. This is the normal steady state and must not read as an error.
A resolution is being recorded; the affected row is busy while others stay actionable.
The queue has not refreshed recently; the age of the data is shown rather than implied.
The queue could not be fetched. The operator is told whether anything is pending is unknown, not shown an empty list.
The caller is not in the operator realm. Approval controls are absent rather than present-and-refusing.
Resolution cannot reach the API; pending resolutions are held rather than silently dropped.
Some data resolved and some did not; the page names which rather than showing a blank.

claims.statement: Amount and counterparty precede every other field in each row's reading order.
Approve and decline are reachable from the list row without navigation.
The empty state is visually and textually distinct from the request-error state.
The request-error state renders dedicated content that says the pending set is unknown.
Every approve and decline control is operable by keyboard with a visible focus state.
Each money-acting control carries an accessible name stating the amount and counterparty.
Request urgency is conveyed by text or shape in addition to colour.
At least three pending requests are readable without scrolling at the desktop baseline.
